title: Coefficient tower operations and point sections
statement:
For any commutative ring $S$ in universe $r$, put $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}S)=\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}S$ and use its standard derived localization, with simultaneous K-injective resolutions, and any fixed derived localization of $\operatorname{Mod}S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Define $\Delta_S$ by localizing the exact ordinary constant-tower functor, $\operatorname{Rlim}_S$ as the total right derived functor of ordinary inverse limit, and $\operatorname{ev}_{S,n}$ by localizing exact evaluation at $n$. Define the adjunction $\Delta_S\dashv\operatorname{Rlim}_S$ by deriving the ordinary constant/limit adjunction, whose counit is the whole limit cone; ordinary inverse limit is additive.

Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with algebraically closed field $k$ in universe $u$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E$ in universe $u$ of $\mathbb Q_\ell$ with $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^{n+1}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_s=\lim_n(A_n)_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Set $R^+=\operatorname{ULift}_{u+1}R$, the existing common coefficient lift for point sections [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness]. Define $\Gamma_\bullet$ on strict $\widehat R_s$-module towers by applying the existing integral point-sections functor at each level, retaining the transitions. This functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits by exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; define its derived functor by exact termwise localization. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, define the natural scalar-restriction comparison
$$\operatorname{Res}_{\widehat R_s\to(A_n)_s}\,;\,\Gamma_R\ \cong\ \Gamma_{A_n}\,;\,\operatorname{Res}_{R^+\to\operatorname{ULift}_{u+1}A_n}$$
using restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the recorded finite and integral point sections [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness]. Its component on every module is the identity on every section at the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$; this property uniquely determines the comparison.
